findings.current: UN Regulation No. 161 — Pedal Misapplication Mitigation Systems
findings.proposed: UN Regulation No. 161 — Devices against Unauthorized Use
findings.evidence: Search result: UN Regulation No. 161 is titled "Devices against Unauthorized Use" - uniform provisions concerning the protection of motor vehicles against unauthorized use and approval of the device against unauthorized use (by means of a locking system); published 25/10/2021.

findings.current: Pedal misapplication mitigation systems are the subject of this regulation...
findings.proposed: UN R161 covers devices against unauthorized use (locking systems) for vehicles; not pedal misapplication.
findings.evidence: Same source as title finding; summary and systems tags (ADAS, Braking) derive from the wrong title. Repo body: "See the UNECE WP.29 Regulations index" only.

findings.current: ["ADAS","Braking"]
findings.proposed: ["Theft prevention"]
findings.evidence: R161 is a device against unauthorized use (locking system), per UNECE title; ADAS/Braking tags follow the wrong title.

findings.current: UN Regulation No. 153 — Fuel System Integrity in a Frontal Collision
findings.proposed: UN Regulation No. 153 — Fuel System Integrity and Safety of Electric Power Train in the Event of a Rear-End Collision
findings.evidence: Search result: "UN Regulation concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to fuel system integrity and safety of electric power train in the event of a rear-end collision"; applies to M1 (<=3,500 kg) and N1; in force 22 Jan 2021; aligns with R34 and R100.

findings.current: ...addresses fuel system integrity in passenger vehicles during a frontal collision...
findings.proposed: Fuel system integrity and high-voltage electric power train safety after a rear-end collision (M1/N1).
findings.evidence: R153 is the rear-end collision regulation, not frontal (frontal fuel/HV safety is covered by R94/R137/R100 pathways).

findings.current: ["Fuel safety","Crashworthiness"]
findings.proposed: add "Battery safety"
findings.evidence: R153 also covers safety of the high-voltage electric power train after rear impact.

findings.current: UN Regulation No. 149 — Road Illumination Devices (except headlamps)
findings.proposed: UN Regulation No. 149 — Road Illumination Devices (RID)
findings.evidence: Search result: R149 "applies to headlamps emitting a driving-beam and/or an asymmetrical passing-beam for vehicles of categories L, M, N and T, adaptive front-lighting systems (AFS)..." i.e. it covers headlamps.

findings.current: Road illumination devices (excluding headlamps) are regulated under UN R149...
findings.proposed: R149 (RID) is the consolidated headlamp regulation: driving/passing-beam headlamps and AFS, replacing R112/R113/R123 etc. for new approvals.
findings.evidence: Search result (Dun-Bri/UNECE): R149 covers headlamps with driving-beam and/or passing-beam and AFS; "unique identifier" etc. Excluding headlamps is the opposite of its scope.

findings.current: UN Regulation No. 100 — Electric Power Trained Vehicles — Construction and Functional Safety
findings.proposed: UN Regulation No. 100 — Vehicles with Regard to Specific Requirements for the Electric Power Train
findings.evidence: Official title: "Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to specific requirements for the electric power train." Record says "Electric Power Trained Vehicles".

findings.current: ...Battery electric and fuel cell vehicles... mandates construction and functional safety...
findings.proposed: Cover vehicles with electric power train (high-voltage bus, REESS safety); R100 Part I vehicle, Part II REESS.
findings.evidence: R100 addresses safety of the electric power train and HV components galvanically connected to the HV bus; "fuel cell vehicles" is not stated in the official title.

findings.current: UN Regulation No. 114 — Airbag Systems
findings.proposed: UN Regulation No. 114 — Replacement Airbag Modules, Replacement Steering Wheels with Airbag and Replacement Airbag Systems
findings.evidence: Official: "approval of: I. An airbag module for a replacement airbag system; II. A replacement steering wheel equipped with an airbag module of an approved type; III. A replacement airbag system other than that installed in a steering wheel." (M1/N1 aftermarket equipment). Title "Airbag Systems" implies OE airbag requirements.

findings.current: Airbag systems are the subject of this UN regulation...
findings.proposed: Applies to replacement (aftermarket) airbag modules/steering wheels/airbag systems for M1 and N1 vehicles.
findings.evidence: Same source: R114 is about replacement airbag equipment, not OE airbag systems generally.

findings.current: ESC systems on passenger cars...
findings.proposed: ESC on M1 and N1 vehicles (passenger cars and light commercial vehicles).
findings.evidence: Search result: "UN Regulation No. 140 applies to the approval of vehicles of category M1 and N1 with regard to their electronic stability control system."

findings.current: UN Regulation No. 150 — Retro-Reflecting Devices (updated)
findings.proposed: UN Regulation No. 150 — Retro-Reflective Devices and Markings (RRD)
findings.evidence: "(updated)" is not part of the title; R150 consolidates retro-reflectors, marking plates, markings and warning triangles (replacing R3, R27, R69, R70, R104).

findings.current: ["Theft prevention","Cybersecurity","Vehicle identification"]
findings.proposed: ["Theft prevention"]
findings.evidence: R116 protects against unauthorized use (locks, immobilizers, alarms); Cybersecurity (R155) is a different regulation.

notes: All 44 records are one-line stubs linking to the generic WP.29 index, so no regulation text is held although UI may present it as full text. Many summaries are meta-statements ('provided text contains only a reference link') that describe the stub rather than the regulation; they should be regenerated. Titles/summaries appear to be generated from memory and some are wrong (R161, R153, R149) - suggests checking titles of adjacent ECE records against the UNECE list. No un_equivalent fields, effective_date or last_amended present on these records. Statuses 'in-force' look right for all; R13/R13-H/R10 etc. are current. Titles for R0, R10, R11, R112, R113, R119, R12, R121, R123, R125, R127, R128, R129, R13, R13-H, R135, R137-R139, R14, R141-R145, R148, R152, R154-R160, R16 matched my knowledge/spot-checks; only R101, R140, R145, R149, R150, R153, R154, R161, R114, R100 were web-checked.
